subject: Multi-year pricing: 3yr lock + uplift cap & renewal protection
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@citrinehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@citrinehealth.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-year pricing ask – 3yr lock + renewal protection

Jonas,

Thanks for the call this morning. Citrine is finalizing our three-year vendor budget and we'd like to surface a firm ask so procurement can present to finance. High level: we want a 3-year price lock at the current 2026 unit rates for the sku set in the attached SOW, an uplift cap on any allowed annual increases (ideally <= 5%), and a renewal-protection clause that provides credits or a true-up if the renewal pricing exceeds the agreed cap.

Key constraints on our side: multi-year commit, predictable unit economics for modeling, and the ability to close by 7/15 to align with our board cycle. We're open to reasonable financial protections on Redwood's side (advance, deposits, or escrow) if that helps. Can you put together a short mutual action plan and what approvals you'd need from your leadership?

Appreciate it — Alex

Attachments: Citrine_SOW_v1.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@citrinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year pricing ask – 3yr lock + renewal protection

Alex — thanks, and great sync earlier. I put together a pragmatic draft that balances Citrine's predictability needs with Redwood's risk profile. Summary below; asking exec review for two non-standard items (discount depth + a commitment reserve mechanism). Full pricing summary attached.

Proposal (draft):
- Term: 36 months; annual committed minimum: $1,200,000
- Price lock: hold current unit rates through the three-year term for committed volumes
- Uplift cap: annual increase capped at 4% year 2, 5% year 3 (cumulative cap not to exceed 9% over base)
- Renewal protection: if published renewal price for the same offering exceeds our uplift schedule by >3 percentage points, Citrine would receive a one-time credit equal to 20% of the first-year committed spend toward the first 12 months after renewal
- Discount: one-time up-front discount of 12% off list for committed volumes (applies to the committed minimum)
- Commitment reserve: hold 10% of the annual committed spend as a credit on Redwood account (applies as a buffer against renewal volatility); refundable against consumption and usable as prepaid credit for services

Two items requiring Exec signoff / Deal Desk exception:
1) Discount level (12%): above standard self-serve discounts for this segment — needs deal desk/exec approval.
2) Commitment reserve (10% held as credit): acceptable operationally but finance/legal want exec blessing for the refundable-credit mechanics and accounting treatment.

Next steps: Ben/Marissa/Laura — can you confirm whether finance and deal desk are comfortable with the above guardrails (discount cap and the commitment-reserve approach)? If so, I'll present for senior approval and loop in Legal for the renewal language. Alex — if this looks directionally right I can turn this into a short amendment + mutual action plan and aim to have exec feedback by EOD.

Thanks,
Jonas

Attachments: DL-2026-0783_pricing_summary.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year pricing ask – 3yr lock + renewal protection

Jonas — thanks for the precise draft. I'm supportive of moving this forward but have two comments from deal desk/ops:

1) Discount: 12% is at the high end for a 3yr commit in this cohort. Recommend we cap the effective discount at 15% only if Citrine pre-pays 12 months up front OR commits to an accelerated payment schedule. Otherwise authorization only up to 10% without prepay.
2) Commitment reserve: I prefer the credit-held approach vs third-party escrow (less legal friction). But we should define a release schedule: 50% of the reserve released after 18 months if consumption tracks >=85% of committed; remainder released pro-rata at renewal.

Also ping Legal for renewal-credit wording — we need a clean metric for measuring "published renewal price" and an explicit trigger for the credit.

Ben

Subject: Re: Multi-year pricing ask – 3yr lock + renewal protection

Folks — quick finance take: I like the structure but please note the following constraints for accounting and cash flow: 

• Effective discount ceiling without additional credit risk mitigation = 10%. Anything above requires a finance sign-off AND a clear collectability plan (prepay, letter of credit, or commitment reserve with defined release conditions).
• Commitment reserve: 10% looks reasonable operationally but we need the following in the term sheet: release milestones (Ben suggested 50% at 18 months), explicit usage rules (only usable against Redwood services), and a reconciliation clause at renewal.
• Renewal credit: define the comparator (we should compare to Redwood list price for the same SKU family published 90 days prior to renewal) and cap the maximum credit to 25% of first-year committed spend.

If Legal signs off on language, I'm OK to escalate for Exec approval with the following packaged ask: 12% discount conditional on either (A) 12-month prepay, or (B) 10% discount + commitment reserve with the release schedule. That gives us flexibility to close ahead of Citrine's board deadline.

Marissa

Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year pricing ask – 3yr lock + renewal protection

Alex — thanks for the quick ask and patience while we threaded internal approvals. Short summary for Citrine:

1) Redwood can commit to a 36-month price lock on committed volumes with a structured uplift schedule (4% Y2, 5% Y3) and a renewal-protection credit if renewal pricing exceeds the uplift band by >3 percentage points.
2) We will offer a path to a 12% one-time discount if Citrine (A) prepays 12 months of committed spend OR (B) agrees to a 10% discount + 10% commitment reserve (held as account credit) with release milestones (50% @ 18 months provided >=85% consumption, remainder at renewal reconciliation).
3) Finance asks that maximum renewal credit be capped at 25% of first-year committed spend and that renewal comparisons use Redwood list price for the same SKU family published 90 days prior to renewal.

Next: I'm taking this package to Exec for signoff this morning (Ben/Marissa/Laura have confirmed the package constraints). I expect a yes/no by lunchtime; if approved, Legal will produce a short amendment and we can target signature by 7/10 to meet Citrine's board timing.

Alex — will follow up within a few hours with the exec decision and the proposed mutual action plan. Thanks again — Jonas
